record.original_question: Let F1, ..., Fs be homogeneous forms of degree d in variables y1, ..., yn, let x1, ..., xs be new variables, and consider the Artinian Gorenstein algebra whose Macaulay inverse system is generated by sum_i x_i^e F_i. Determine, for general values of e and for specific choices of the forms F_i, when this Gorenstein algebra has the weak Lefschetz property and when it has the strong Lefschetz property.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.7. To determine whether the Gorenstein algebra given by Σ x^e_iFi has the WLP and/or the SLP.

In terms of Macaulay inverse systems, we can construct the idealization of the canonical module of an Artinian level algebra with inverse system ⟨F1, F2, . . . , Fs⟩ as the Gorenstein algebra with inverse system ⟨Σ xiFi⟩ where x1, x2, . . . , xs are new variables. Here the forms F1, . . . , Fs are assumed to be homogeneous of degree d in variables y1, y2, . . . , yn. Preliminary studies of the Gorenstein algebra given by ⟨Σ x^e_iFi⟩ show that for e ≥ d it satisfies the WLP for any forms Fi while for e < d we have examples failing the WLP and examples satisfying the WLP.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero and consider the polynomial ring $R = k[y_1,\dots,y_n,x_1,\dots,x_s]$. Fix a positive integer $d$ and homogeneous forms $F_1,\dots,F_s \in k[y_1,\dots,y_n]$ each of degree $d$, and fix a nonnegative integer $e$. Form the homogeneous polynomial
$$G_e \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{s} x_i^{\,e}\,F_i(y_1,\dots,y_n) \;\in\; R,$$
and let $A_e = R/\mathrm{Ann}(G_e)$ be the standard graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra whose Macaulay inverse system is generated by $G_e$ (where $R$ acts on the polynomial ring in dual variables by contraction/differentiation).

Recall that a standard graded Artinian algebra $A = \bigoplus_{i=0}^D A_i$ has the Weak Lefschetz Property (WLP) if there exists a linear form $\ell \in A_1$ such that the multiplication map $\times \ell : A_i \to A_{i+1}$ has maximal rank for every $i$, and has the Strong Lefschetz Property (SLP) if there exists $\ell \in A_1$ such that $\times \ell^k : A_i \to A_{i+k}$ has maximal rank for every $i$ and every $k \geq 1$.

Determine, as functions of the integer $e$ and of the choice of the forms $F_1,\dots,F_s$:
(a) precisely when the Gorenstein algebra $A_e$ has the Weak Lefschetz Property; and
(b) precisely when the Gorenstein algebra $A_e$ has the Strong Lefschetz Property.

In particular, characterize the behavior for general $e$ (e.g. for $e \geq d$ versus $e < d$) and for specific natural families of forms $F_i$ (such as monomials, powers of linear forms, or generic forms).
artifact.status_search_result: The question of when these "generalized Nagata idealization" Gorenstein algebras with inverse system $\sum x_i^e F_i$ satisfy WLP/SLP is an active area of research. Partial results are known: WLP is proved in some ranges (e.g. when the exponent on $x_i$ is at least $d$, or for certain Nagata idealizations of order $d_1\geq d_2$), and families of Perazzo-type Gorenstein algebras (special cases of this construction) failing WLP have been constructed. A complete characterization in terms of $e$ and the forms $F_i$ does not appear in the literature, so the problem remains open in general, with only partial results.

status_evidence.title: Roller Coaster Gorenstein algebras and Koszul algebras failing the weak Lefschetz property
status_evidence.snippet: Roller Coaster artinian Gorenstein algebras are in fact Perazzo algebras, arising from Nagata idealizations of monomial algebras... family of G-quadratic Perazzo algebras failing the weak Lefschetz property.
status_evidence.claim: Examples of Gorenstein algebras from Nagata idealizations failing WLP are still being constructed; the WLP/SLP question for such families is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Lefschetz Properties for CW-complex Nagata Idealizations
status_evidence.snippet: WLP holds for Nagata idealizations of order d1 when d1 >= d2.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial sufficient conditions for WLP for Nagata-type idealizations are known.
